sentences.text:
Asis Joardar & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 13
March, 2024
Author: Suvra Ghosh

Bench: Suvra Ghosh
March 13, 2024
 Ardr (687)
 Wpa 26579 of 2023
 Asis Joardar & anr.
 Vs.
 The State of West Bengal & ors.

Adv. Debdutta Basu,
 ...petitioners.

Adv. Chandi Charan De,
 Adv. Anirban Sarkar,
 ...for the State.
On prayer of the petitioners the name of the 8 th  respondent be expunged from the cause title of the writ petition.
The cause title of the writ petition be amended accordingly.
Affidavit of service filed by the petitioners is taken on record.
None appears for the 6th and 7th respondents despite service.

It is submitted on behalf of the petitioners that upon demise of the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners who was the owner of the land in question, the pro-forma respondents who are the sisters of the petitioners have gifted the land in favour of the petitioners vide deeds dated 16th November, 2021.

Upon acquiring title in respect of the entire plot, the petitioners conducted measurement of the plot by a surveyor and found that the quantum of land in possession of the petitioners is 0.06 acres less than the quantum recorded in the record of rights.
Pursuant to an order passed by this Court in WPA 15907 of 2022 on 11 th November, 2022, the petitioners submitted a representation in this regard before the concerned authority.

The concerned authority,
being the District Magistrate, Nadia disposed of the representation submitted by the petitioners by an order passed on 3 rd August, 2023 turning down the claim of the petitioners.
The said order is impugned in the present application.

sentences.text: It has been admitted by the authority that the father of the petitioners was the erstwhile owner of the land in question which has been utilised by the authorities by construction of a road therein before about 30-35 years.

Strangely, the District Magistrate has observed that since the petitioners'
father did not raise any objection against such utilisation, it may be presumed that he voluntarily allowed the respondents to use the land for the benefit of the public.
Also, since no objection was raised by the original owner of the land, the petitioners were not entitled to raise objection after passage of 30-35 years.
Such observation is unknown to law.
It is trite law that that in case of a continuing cause of action, the land losers cannot be deprived of compensation merely because of passage of time.

Since admittedly the land of the petitioners has been utilised by the authority by constructing a road therein, it is incumbent upon the authority to either compensate the petitioners in terms of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 or propose direct purchase of the land from the petitioners at the present market rate.

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Since the 6th and 7th respondents who have admittedly utilised the land in question are not represented, the petitioners are directed to serve notice upon the said respondents intimating the adjourned date.
Let the matter appear under the same heading on 12th April, 2024.

(Suvra Ghosh, J.)
